_note: Labeled (narrative, technique_id, should_match) pairs used to calibrate the AttackClassifier's similarity threshold via Youden's J statistic. 16 positive + 16 negative pairs.

pairs.narrative: An IAM role was granted a wildcard administrator policy attaching full access to all AWS services, allowing the identity to modify permissions for any other account in the environment.
A new IAM user was created with programmatic access keys shortly after a suspicious login, providing a fallback identity independent of the originally compromised account.
Multi-factor authentication was disabled on a privileged account and the account's trust policy was widened to accept assumption from any principal in the organization.
A low-privilege role assumed a highly permissive deployment role via a broad AssumeRole trust relationship, gaining administrative control over production resources.
An organization-wide service control policy was modified to remove a restriction on root account usage, weakening guardrails across every account in the tenant.
CloudTrail logging was disabled in a region immediately before a large number of security group changes were made, removing the audit trail for those changes.
An EC2 snapshot was copied to an external account and the original instance was terminated shortly afterward, removing traces of the compromised workload.
CloudTrail log files for the past week were deleted from the logging bucket, and log file validation was turned off to prevent detection of the tampering.
AWS access keys were found hardcoded in a public GitHub repository and were used minutes later to authenticate from an unfamiliar IP address.
A secrets manager vault containing database credentials and API keys was accessed by a role that had never previously read from that vault.
Dozens of MFA push notifications were sent to a user's device within a few minutes from a session that already held valid primary credentials.
An unfamiliar identity called ListBuckets, ListObjects, and DescribeInstances across every region in the account within a short burst, mapping out the environment's storage and compute resources.
A role with no prior storage access listed the contents of a customer data bucket and then downloaded a large number of individual objects from it, accessing data outside its normal baseline.
A large volume of objects was copied from a production storage bucket into a bucket owned by an unrelated external AWS account, moving the data outside of organizational control.
Every object in a production database table was deleted within seconds by an automated script, and the delete operation was not preceded by any backup or export activity.
All backup snapshots and point-in-time recovery settings for a database were disabled shortly before the primary tables were encrypted and became inaccessible to normal users.
A developer created a new S3 bucket for a personal project and left the default encryption settings unchanged during routine business hours.
A routine scheduled compliance scan queried the encryption configuration of every S3 bucket in the account, as it does every morning at 9 AM.
An engineer updated the color scheme of the internal dashboard application and pushed the change through the normal CI/CD pipeline.
A scheduled Lambda function ran its usual nightly job of aggregating daily metrics and writing a summary report to a reporting bucket.
A new employee's IAM user was provisioned through the standard onboarding automation with read-only access to the shared documentation wiki.
The security team rotated an old access key as part of a routine 90-day credential rotation policy and updated the corresponding secret in the vault.
A quarterly access review confirmed that an IAM role's permissions still matched its documented purpose and no changes were required.
An application health check pinged the CloudWatch Logs API every minute to confirm log delivery was functioning normally.
A backup job ran on schedule, creating a new snapshot of the production database and verifying the previous three snapshots were still retained.
A support engineer viewed the billing dashboard to check the current month's spend across services, as part of a routine cost review.
A CI pipeline assumed its designated deployment role, which it does on every merge to main, and pushed a new container image to the registry.
The on-call engineer manually re-enabled a security group rule that had been accidentally removed during a maintenance window earlier that day.
A data analyst ran a scheduled export of an internal reporting table to a shared analytics bucket used by the finance team every Friday.
An automated test suite created and deleted several temporary EC2 instances as part of its normal integration test run.
The IT helpdesk reset a user's password after a forgotten-password request submitted through the normal self-service portal.
A monitoring agent queried the list of running containers on a cluster once per minute as part of its standard health-check cycle.
